sources.title: JPL satellite mean elements
sources.evidence: Ephemeris and mean-element route checked; live table is dynamic. No new fit or validity interval was qualified.

sources.title: JPL satellite physical parameters
sources.evidence: Physical-parameter catalog checked as a size/reference route; a catalog radius alone does not establish a shape.

sources.title: PDS Voyager ISS archive
sources.evidence: Mission archive route checked against package-specific observation records. Nominal target center and actual body intersection differ.
sources.scope: Voyager observations; individual frame selection is in each package source record

sources.title: Schenk and Moore Uranian satellite maps
sources.evidence: Repository source records and pinned release README were read; external repository endpoint did not open in this pass. Maps and DEM coverage differ by body.
sources.scope: Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon, Miranda mosaics; selected terrain models

sources.title: Miranda digitized geology lead
sources.evidence: Lead is explicitly recorded in the inspected Miranda package. External access unresolved; projection, content and reuse have not been qualified.

sources.title: Titania geologic investigation
sources.evidence: Deblurring and geologic interpretation are a useful research lead. Package records loss of geospatial information; no drop-in registered map was qualified.

sources.title: Geologic map of Oberon catalog record
sources.evidence: Interpretive map lead checked; no reusable registered raster was qualified.

sources.title: Karkoschka 2001 Uranian satellite shapes
sources.evidence: Published projected/prolate shape fits underpin the individually inspected inner-moon packages; equal minor axes are a model assumption.
sources.scope: Cordelia, Ophelia, Bianca, Cressida, Desdemona, Juliet, Portia, Rosalind, Belinda

sources.title: Uranian ring occultations and inner-moon constraints
sources.evidence: Revised dynamical/occultation constraints are distinct from measured three-dimensional terrain. Package-specific uncertainty interpretations were checked.

sources.title: Hedman et al. spectral trends across Uranian and Neptunian rings and small moons
sources.evidence: NIRCam disk-integrated photometry and observation tables were read, including Cupid, Perdita, Mab and Hippocamp. These are spectra, not mapped surface textures.
sources.scope: Specifically verified missing targets: Cupid, Perdita, Mab, Hippocamp; broader listed inner moons

sources.title: French et al. HST inner Uranian satellite analysis
sources.evidence: Poster gives individual astrometry and photometry, including Cupid/Puck hemispheric asymmetry. Belinda/Perdita resonance fit is explicitly still in progress.
sources.scope: Named table rows: Ophelia, Cressida, Desdemona, Juliet, Portia, Rosalind, Cupid, Belinda, Perdita, Puck, Mab

sources.title: Farkas-Takacs et al. Uranian irregular moons with K2, Herschel and Spitzer
sources.evidence: Table 4 supplies measured photometric periods/amplitudes for five detections; thermal constraints differ by target. Stephano and Trinculo yielded no meaningful K2 signal.
sources.scope: Detected: Caliban, Sycorax, Prospero, Setebos, Ferdinand; nondetections: Stephano, Trinculo

sources.title: Maris et al. VLT Uranian irregular photometry
sources.evidence: Independent colors and variability study; abstract and target membership checked, not a unique shape inversion.

sources.title: Uranian irregular satellites physical summary and occultation prospects
sources.evidence: Table individually reconciles all nine pre-2023 irregulars. Predicted occultations are prospects, not measured silhouettes.
sources.scope: Caliban, Sycorax, Prospero, Setebos, Stephano, Trinculo, Francisco, Margaret, Ferdinand

sources.title: Sheppard 2024 ultra-deep Uranus and Neptune satellite surveys
sources.evidence: Discovery imaging and astrometry establish three exact new aliases; brightness-derived dimensions depend on assumed albedo.

sources.title: Subaru three new moons discovery report
sources.evidence: Observatory account confirms discovery/recovery epochs for the three survey moons.

sources.title: Webb discovery of S/2025 U1
sources.evidence: NIRCam program 6379, February 2025 observations; roughly 10 km is an estimate, not resolved axes.

sources.title: PDS Uranian satellite parameters
sources.evidence: Perdita, Mab and Cupid size entries individually checked; diameters are not shape products.

sources.title: Kiss et al. Nereid thermal and rotational properties
sources.evidence: The package uses one illustrative member of an inferred ellipsoid family, not a uniquely determined mesh/pole.

sources.title: Karkoschka 2003 sizes and shapes of Neptune inner satellites
sources.evidence: Image-derived axes are recorded individually by existing packages; they are analytic approximations, not surface models.

sources.title: PDS Stooke small-body shape models
sources.evidence: Actual collection membership checked: Larissa and Proteus included; Dactyl and Puck are not listed. Ida is a different body from Dactyl.
sources.scope: Includes Larissa, Proteus, Ida and other explicitly named bodies

sources.title: USGS Triton controlled mosaic
sources.evidence: Existing package pins the controlled monochrome product and resolves conflicting meridian prose using file labels.

sources.title: LPI Triton color map
sources.evidence: Existing package uses the enhanced-color release with explicit coverage/processing limits.

sources.title: Brozovic et al. 2011 Neptune outer satellite orbits
sources.evidence: Author institution abstract identifies all five targets and state-vector/orbital-fit publication; observations extend arcs to 2009.

sources.title: Sheppard et al. Neptune irregular survey
sources.evidence: Discovery of Psamathe and comparison with S/2002 N4; size estimates use assumed reflectivity.

sources.title: Maris et al. multicolor photometry of Neso
sources.evidence: VRI photometry is reported with large errors; six hours were insufficient for a meaningful rotational period.

sources.title: Showalter et al. discovery and analysis of Hippocamp
sources.evidence: HST discovery, astrometry and conditional radius are reported. Intermediate image archive is linked; no measured three-axis shape.
sources.scope: Hippocamp; updated observations of other inner Neptunian moons

sources.title: Showalter intermediate HST analysis data
sources.evidence: Actual data-availability link in the paper; file inventory/bytes were not inspected.
sources.scope: Hippocamp HST observations and analysis intermediates

sources.title: USGS Charon global mosaic
sources.evidence: Existing package pins monochrome mosaic and companion topography relative to a 606 km sphere.

sources.title: PDS New Horizons derived global color and absorption maps overview
sources.evidence: Release overview explicitly distinguishes global maps for Pluto/Charon from target image cubes including Nix, Hydra, Kerberos. MVIC bands require calibration.
sources.scope: Charon mapped products; Nix, Hydra, Kerberos image cubes

sources.title: Porter Nix shape model v1
sources.evidence: Public fitted mesh, already pinned in package; fitted image registration is not supplied.

sources.title: Porter Hydra shape model v1
sources.evidence: Public fitted mesh, already pinned in package; poorly seen south and missing camera registration constrain use.

sources.title: Porter et al. Pluto small-moon fits
sources.evidence: New fits and initial albedo work were presented; no associated downloadable new mesh plus fitted camera transforms was identified in the checked presentation.

sources.title: Hiʻiaka stellar occultations and shape
sources.evidence: Reported semi-axes 240±40, 180±30, 143±7 km are a model from occultations/photometry, not full diameters or a terrain mesh. Article footer CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

sources.title: Hiʻiaka paper Source Data workbook
sources.evidence: Workbook is actually linked by the paper; download bytes were inaccessible in this pass. Selection-specific reuse/attribution terms remain to inspect.

sources.title: Non-Keplerian Haumea satellite orbits
sources.evidence: Interacting satellite fit and primary gravity replace an independent two-body interpretation.

sources.title: Haumea system thermal revision
sources.evidence: System thermal interpretation includes satellites; estimated sizes/albedos are not individual shapes.

sources.title: Brown and Butler 2023 ALMA Eris/Orcus satellite study
sources.evidence: Resolved thermal and astrometric constraints supply component information, not terrain; Dysnomia mass limit and Vanth mass ratio differ.

sources.title: Holler et al. Dysnomia orbit
sources.evidence: Additional HST epochs break prior orbit-pole degeneracy; moon spin/shape are separate unknowns.

sources.title: Bamberger et al. preliminary Makemake satellite orbit
sources.evidence: 2015–2019 HST detections yield preliminary approximately 18-day circular orbit; not a resolved shape.

sources.title: Discovery of the satellite of 2007 OR10
sources.evidence: HST observations resolve the pair as sources, not the satellite surface; identity predates Gonggong/Xiangliu names.

sources.title: Mass and density of dwarf planet 2007 OR10
sources.evidence: Satellite orbit fit supports system mass; mirror-orbit/size assumptions remain relevant.

sources.title: Beyond Point Masses V: Weywot orbit
sources.evidence: Non-Keplerian fit includes Quaoar figure and photocenter effects; inferred low eccentricity differs from older solutions.

sources.title: Sickafoose et al. Vanth stellar occultation
sources.evidence: Occultation gives a size constraint with a spherical-limb assumption; chords involve different stars and do not determine a full 3D figure.

sources.title: Collyer et al. Salacia-Actaea rotation and orbit
sources.evidence: Long photometry plus resolved HST constrain orbit/synchronous interpretation. Dominant system light-curve variation belongs to Salacia, not a measured Actaea shape.

sources.title: Grundy et al. Varda-Ilmarë mutual orbit
sources.evidence: Resolved astrometry/component photometry determine mutual orbit; thermal area partition and albedo assumptions do not resolve Ilmarë shape.

sources.title: Veverka et al. Dactyl morphology and photometry
sources.evidence: 47 Galileo images at 18 epochs; full dimensions about 1.6×1.4×1.2 km, best monochrome tens of metres/pixel.

sources.title: Levison et al. a contact binary satellite of Dinkinesh
sources.evidence: Lucy observations establish Selam contact-binary morphology; parent Dinkinesh shape must not be assigned to Selam.

sources.title: Lucy Dinkinesh/Selam geology study
sources.evidence: Primary institutional manuscript located; full final file retrieval failed. Observed companion mesh release remains unresolved.

sources.title: Selam formation study data availability
sources.evidence: Paper explicitly links Lucy L’LORRI Dinkinesh partially processed collection; simulation archive is distinct from measured companion geometry.

sources.title: PDS Lucy L’LORRI Dinkinesh partially processed v1
sources.evidence: Actual release link identified via data-availability statement (DOI 10.26007/kvc4-2t38); bytes/labels not acquired.

sources.title: PDS JPL radar shape model collection
sources.evidence: Collection explicitly includes 1999 KW4 Alpha and Beta; Beta is Squannit, not Moshup. DOI 10.26033/xtkf-wz81.

sources.title: PDS JPL radar shape data directory
sources.evidence: Inventory explicitly lists a66391_1999kw4_secondary.obj/.xml and a66391_beta_spin_state.csv/.xml. Individual bytes not decoded in this pass.
sources.scope: Squannit actual OBJ and spin-state release

sources.title: Kalliope-Linus occultations and transits analysis
sources.evidence: Detailed parent model plus Linus transit/occultation constraints; Linus is modeled as a sphere, not delivered as measured terrain.

sources.title: Daphne internal structure and Peneius orbit
sources.evidence: Table 3 gives Genoid satellite fit from AO observations; detailed reconstructed shape belongs to Daphne.

sources.title: Dynamics of the triple asteroid Eugenia
sources.evidence: Outer named moon and inner provisional moon are distinguished; resolved positions and brightness estimates do not supply a Petit-Prince terrain mesh.

sources.title: Berthier et al. Sylvia physical/dynamical properties
sources.evidence: Romulus occultation projected area-equivalent diameter 23.1±0.7 km and projected axis ratio 2.7±0.3; unknown third dimension.

sources.title: Sylvia system updated shape, occultations and orbits
sources.evidence: Updated moon astrometry/occultation constraints; released detailed shape is Sylvia, not automatically either moon.

sources.title: Broz et al. non-Keplerian Kleopatra moon orbits
sources.evidence: Multipole/N-body orbital solution; detailed primary shape is not a companion mesh.

sources.title: Brown et al. orbit of Queta
sources.evidence: HST orbital fit and faint companion photometry; size assumes reflectivity.

sources.title: Marchis et al. puzzling mutual orbit of Hektor
sources.evidence: Satellite orbit is eccentric/inclined; bilobed reconstructed primary is Hektor, not its moon.

sources.title: Buie et al. Patroclus-Menoetius occultation
sources.evidence: Six-chord Menoetius projected limb is 117.2×93 km; light-curve combination infers a 3D axis ratio, not directly measured terrain.
